targets.authors: Yi P, Park JS, Melton DA.
targets.title: Betatrophin: a hormone that controls pancreatic β cell proliferation.
targets.evidence_quote: First, we established that immunodeficient NOD-Scid (NOD.CB17-Prkdc scid /J) mice respond to the insulin receptor inhibitor S961 in a fashion similar to that seen by Yi et al. ( 9 ) in C57BL/6J mice.
targets.outcome_quote: Messenger RNA levels of betatrophin were induced about fivefold as determined by quantitative RT-PCR ( Fig. 1 B ), similar to what was published previously for C57BL/6 mice ( 9 ). However, betatrophin mRNA levels were not increased in gonadal white adipose tissue after S961 treatment as had been reported by Yi et al. ( 9 ), possibly due to the different mouse strains used or fat depots analyzed ( Fig. 1 C ). It is worth noting that the increase in adipose tissue betatrophin mRNA reported previously was not statistically significant ( 9 ).
targets.outcome_reasoning: Mouse pancreatic proliferation and liver expression agree with Yi et al.; the authors explicitly contrast the adipose-expression result with that original. Under the codebook a tested finding explicitly contrasted cannot be omitted. Human islet nonresponse is an extension to a species whose response the introduction says was previously unknown; it is not itself evidence of failure to replicate a previously established human finding.

reasoning: Fresh mouse/islet data directly check Yi et al.'s published mouse effects and extend to human islets. Other references supply background or methods, not additional retested published findings.
